# fleet

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/pwinskill/fleet/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pwinskill/fleet/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![pkgdown](https://github.com/pwinskill/fleet/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pwinskill/fleet/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml)
[![Lifecycle:
experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![License:
MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](https://github.com/pwinskill/fleet/blob/main/LICENSE.md)

`fleet` is a deterministic mean-field counterpart to the
[malariasimulation](https://github.com/mrc-ide/malariasimulation)
individual-based model (IBM) of *Plasmodium falciparum* and *P. vivax*
malaria. It takes an unmodified `malariasimulation` parameter list, is
seeded at the `malariaEquilibrium` (or `malariaEquilibriumVivax`)
solution as the IBM is, advances one day at a time in the IBM’s order,
and returns the IBM’s output table, so post-processing written for the
IBM, including [postie](https://github.com/mrc-ide/postie), works
unchanged.

The human model is the Griffin-style model, structured by age and biting
heterogeneity, and for *P. vivax* the White-style model with hypnozoite
batches and relapse; both are coupled to the compartmental mosquito
model. `fleet` is written in [odin2](https://github.com/mrc-ide/odin2)
and [dust2](https://github.com/mrc-ide/dust2). Compartments are
per-capita densities, so run time does not depend on population size: a
30-year falciparum run takes about 2 s on one core. The intended uses
are calibration, parameter sweeps and scenario work for which the IBM is
too slow. Use the IBM when you need stochastic variation or individual
heterogeneity beyond the mean field.

## Not ready for real use

`fleet` is a work in progress and is not validated for research, policy
or operational use. It is published so that the approach and its
comparison with `malariasimulation` can be examined, not so that its
numbers can be relied on.

- The API is unstable. The signature of
  [`run_simulation_ode()`](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/reference/run_simulation_ode.md)
  has changed once and may change again without deprecation.
- Known discrepancies with the IBM are open. On the country site files
  `fleet` runs above the IBM on falciparum clinical and severe
  incidence, and further above it on *P. vivax* sites; neither excess is
  explained. Treat severe incidence, and anything derived from it such
  as DALYs, as indicative only.
- Nothing has been peer reviewed, and there is no versioned release.

The current verdict on each comparison is in
[fleetcheck](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleetcheck/). For results that
must be defensible now, use `malariasimulation`.

## Installation

`fleet` and several of its dependencies compile C++ at install time, so
a C++ toolchain is needed: Rtools on Windows, the Xcode command line
tools on macOS, or `r-base-dev` or equivalent on Linux.

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("pwinskill/fleet")
```

This also installs the hard dependencies that are only on GitHub
(`dust2`, `monty`, `malariaEquilibrium` and `malariaEquilibriumVivax`),
through `Remotes` in `DESCRIPTION`. It installs nothing from `Suggests`.
The examples need two suggested packages, `malariasimulation` to build
parameter lists and `postie` to post-process the output:

``` r

remotes::install_github(c("mrc-ide/malariasimulation", "mrc-ide/postie"))
```

## Usage

``` r

library(fleet)

# Output age bands are set on the parameter list, as for the IBM. The defaults
# give 2-10 prevalence and no incidence.
bands <- list(min = c(0, 5, 15) * 365, max = c(5, 15, 100) * 365 - 1)
p <- malariasimulation::get_parameters(list(
  clinical_incidence_rendering_min_ages = bands$min,
  clinical_incidence_rendering_max_ages = bands$max,
  severe_incidence_rendering_min_ages = bands$min,
  severe_incidence_rendering_max_ages = bands$max))

# 10 years, one row per day, in malariasimulation's columns
out <- run_simulation_ode(timesteps = 3650, parameters = malariasimulation::set_equilibrium(p, init_EIR = 20))

# post-processed as for an IBM run
postie::get_prevalence(out, diagnostic = "lm")$lm_prevalence_2_10
postie::get_rates(out)[, c("time", "age_lower", "age_upper", "clinical", "severe", "dalys")]
```

Interventions are added with the usual `malariasimulation::set_*()`
functions and read from the parameter list;
[`run_simulation_ode()`](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/reference/run_simulation_ode.md)
has no extra arguments for them. A list from
`get_parameters(parasite = "vivax")` runs the *P. vivax* model.

The package exports three functions:
[`run_simulation_ode()`](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/reference/run_simulation_ode.md)
runs the model,
[`ode_tuning()`](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/reference/ode_tuning.md)
holds the discretisation settings, and
[`default_age_lower()`](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/reference/default_age_lower.md)
gives the default age grid. The `ode` in two of the names is kept for
compatibility; the model is a daily update, not an ODE.

## Documentation

- [Get started](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/articles/fleet.html):
  running the model, reading the output with `postie`, interventions,
  demography, seasonality and *P. vivax*.
- [Usage notes](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/articles/using.html):
  where the mean field departs from the IBM and what to do about it, and
  run times.
- [Model
  specification](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/articles/model.html):
  scope, the state space and the full daily update.
- [Parameter
  reference](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/articles/parameters.html):
  how `fleet` handles every `malariasimulation` `set_*()` argument:
  exactly, approximately, or not at all.
- [Function
  reference](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/reference/index.html).
- [Contributing](https://github.com/pwinskill/fleet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

Agreement with the IBM is assessed in a separate project,
[fleetcheck](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleetcheck/): a register of
claims covering core relationships, age structure, demography,
interventions and 63 country site files, each with the criterion that
decides it, the value measured against it and a verdict. It records the
evidence so far, failing claims included, and is not a completed
validation. It is kept outside this repository so that the evidence
cannot fall out of date unnoticed alongside the code it assesses, and
this README quotes no comparison figures.

# Package index

## Run the model

Run the mean-field model on a `malariasimulation` parameter list.

- [`run_simulation_ode()`](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/reference/run_simulation_ode.md)
  : Run the mean-field model

## Discretisation settings

The age grid, the prophylaxis chains’ stage counts, the mosquito
sub-steps per day and the *P. vivax* hypnozoite levels. Every default is
the validated choice.

- [`ode_tuning()`](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/reference/ode_tuning.md)
  : Discretisation settings
- [`default_age_lower()`](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/reference/default_age_lower.md)
  : Default age grid

## Package overview

- [`fleet`](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/reference/fleet-package.md)
  [`fleet-package`](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/reference/fleet-package.md)
  : fleet: mean-field counterpart to malariasimulation
